:::{#exm-continuous-rv}
#### A continuous random variable

Let $X$ satisfy $\Pr(a \le X \le b) = b - a$ for all $0 \le a \le b \le 1$.
Taking

$$
\begin{aligned}
a &= b \\
&= x
\end{aligned}
$$

gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(X = x) &= x - x \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

for every $x \in [0,1]$.
Taking $a = 0$ and $b = 1$ gives $\Pr(0 \le X \le 1) = 1$,
so by the [complement rule](probability-basics.qmd#cor-p-neg0)
$X$ falls outside $[0, 1]$ with probability 0,
and $\Pr(X = x) = 0$ for every $x$ outside $[0, 1]$ as well.
So $X$ is continuous.
Its range, $[0, 1]$, is uncountable.

:::
